title.zh: 卷444 列傳二百三十一 黄体芳 宗室宝廷 宗室盛昱 张佩伦 邓承修 徐致祥
title.en: Volume 444 Biographies 231: Huang Tifang, Zong Shibaoting, Zong Shishengyu, Zhang Peilun, Deng Chengxiu, Xu Zhixiang
title.raw: 卷444 列傳二百三十一 黄体芳 宗室宝廷 宗室盛昱 张佩伦 邓承修 徐致祥

sentences.zh: 黃體芳，字漱蘭，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Huang Tifang, courtesy name Shulan, was a man of Rui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tifang, whose courtesy name was Shulan, came from Rui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an editor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tongzhi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as an editor.

sentences.zh: 日探討掌故，慨然有經世志。

translations.literal: Each day he investigated institutional precedents and was stirred with the ambition to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days studying state institutions and came to harbor a strong desire to put his learning to practical service.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，頻上書言時政得失。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and frequently submitted memorials on the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Rising eventually to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, he repeatedly memorialized the throne on the strengths and failings of contemporary governance.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，請籌急賑，整吏治，清庶獄，稱旨。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he requested urgent relief funds, rectification of official conduct, and clearing of ordinary legal cases, and won imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he urged emergency relief, reform of local administration, and review of routine legal cases—measures that met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 時議禁燒鍋裕民食，戶部覈駁，體芳謂燒鍋領帖，部獲歲銀三萬，因上董恂奸邪狀，坐鐫級。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over banning distilleries to spare grain for the people; the Board of Revenue rejected the proposal. Tifang said distillers held licensed permits and the ministry received thirty thousand taels of silver yearly, and he therefore memorialized the wickedness of Dong Xun and was punished by demotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated banning distilleries to free grain for the populace, the Board of Revenue blocked the move. Tifang pointed out that licensed distillers paid the ministry thirty thousand taels a year; he then denounced Dong Xun's corruption and was demoted as punishment.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年三月，惠陵禮成，主事吳可讀為定大統以屍諫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Guangxu, when the rites at Huiling were completed, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup remonstrated with his corpse to fix the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangxu 5, after the rites at Emperor Tongzhi's Huiling mausoleum were completed, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup committed suicide in memorial protest to settle the question of imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 詔言：「同治十三年十二月初五日降旨，嗣後皇帝生有皇子，即承繼大行皇帝為嗣。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "On the fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Tongzhi an order was issued that hereafter, when the emperor bears a son, that son shall succeed the late emperor as heir.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "On the fifth day of the twelfth month, Tongzhi 13, it was decreed that whenever the reigning emperor should have a son, that son would succeed the late emperor as heir.

sentences.zh: 吳可讀所奏，前旨即是此意。」

translations.literal: What Wu Kedup memorialized is exactly the meaning of the earlier edict."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedup's memorial expressed precisely what the earlier edict had meant."

sentences.zh: 於是下群臣議，體芳略言：「'即是此意'一語，止有恪遵，更有何議？

translations.literal: Thereupon the court ordered the ministers to deliberate. Tifang stated in brief: "The phrase 'exactly this meaning' allows only reverent compliance—what further debate is there?
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the ministers to deliberate. Tifang wrote in summary: "The words 'exactly this meaning' permit nothing but obedient compliance—what room is left for argument?

sentences.zh: 乃激烈者盛氣力爭，巽畏者囁嚅不吐，或忠或謹，皆人臣盛節，而惜其未明今日事勢也。

translations.literal: Yet the impassioned contended with full vigor, while the timid murmured and would not speak out; whether loyal or cautious, all showed the utmost integrity of subjects, yet it is regrettable that they did not understand today's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ardent argued with fierce passion while the timid muttered and held back; whether loyal or cautious, each showed the highest integrity of a minister—yet none, alas, grasped the realities of the present moment.

sentences.zh: 譬諸士民之家，長子次子各有孫，而自祖父母視之則無異。

translations.literal: Compare it to a gentry or common household: the eldest and second sons each have grandsons, yet to the grandparents there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Take an ordinary household: the eldest and second sons may each have grandsons, yet to the grandparents those grandchildren are alike.

sentences.zh: 然襲爵職必歸之長房者，嫡長與嫡次之別也。

translations.literal: Yet the hereditary title and office must pass to the senior line—that is the distinction between the legitimate eldest and the legitimate second.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the hereditary title must pass to the senior line—that is the difference between the legitimate eldest son and the legitimate second.

sentences.zh: 又如大宗無子，次宗止一嫡子，然小宗以嫡子繼大宗，不聞有所吝者，以仍得兼承本宗故也。

translations.literal: Again, if the major line has no son and the minor line has only one legitimate son, the minor line's legitimate son may succeed the major line, and one never hears of reluctance, because he may still jointly inherit his own line.
translations.idiomatic: Or again: when the major line lacks an heir and the minor line has but one legitimate son, that son from the minor line may succeed the major line without objection, because he can still inherit his birth line as well.

sentences.zh: 唯君與民微有不同。

translations.literal: Only between sovereign and subject is there a slight difference.
translations.idiomatic: Between throne and subject, however, the case differs slightly.

sentences.zh: 民間以嫡子繼大宗，則大宗為主，本宗為兼。

translations.literal: Among the people, when a legitimate son succeeds the major line, the major line is primary and the birth line secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Among common families, when a legitimate son succeeds the major line, the major line is primary and his birth line secondary.

sentences.zh: 天潢以嫡子繼帝系，則帝係為主，本宗可得而兼，親不可得而兼。

translations.literal: In the imperial clan, when a legitimate son succeeds the imperial line, the imperial line is primary; the birth line may be jointly borne, but the bond of kinship cannot be jointly borne.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial legitimate son succeeds the dynastic line, the dynastic line is primary: he may still hold his birth line in name, but he cannot hold two bonds of filial kinship at once.

sentences.zh: 若人君以嫡子繼長支，則固以繼長支為主，而本宗亦不能不兼。

translations.literal: If a ruler's legitimate son succeeds the senior branch, he must take succession to the senior branch as primary, yet cannot but also bear the birth line jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When a sovereign's legitimate son succeeds the senior imperial branch, succession to that branch is primary—yet he must also bear his birth line jointly.

sentences.zh: 蓋人君無小宗，即稱謂加以區別，亦於本宗恩義無傷。

translations.literal: For a ruler has no minor line; even if titles of address are distinguished, the grace and obligation of the birth line are not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler has no true minor line: even when forms of address are distinguished, the moral claims of his birth line remain intact.

sentences.zh: 此兩宮意在嗣子承統，慈愛穆宗，亦即所以慈愛皇上之說也。

translations.literal: This is what the two palaces mean in wishing an heir's son to bear the succession: to cherish Emperor Muzong is also the way to cherish the present emperor.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the two empress dowagers intend—that an heir's son should carry on the line: to honor Emperor Tongzhi is also to honor the present emperor.

sentences.zh: 今非合兩統為一統，以不定為豫定，就將來承繼者以為承嗣，似亦無策以處之矣。

translations.literal: Now, unless the two successions are united into one, treating what is unsettled as already settled and taking the future successor as the present heir, there seems no way to handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the two lines of succession are merged into one—treating what is still unsettled as already settled and naming the future heir as present heir—there seems no way to resolve the difficulty.

sentences.zh: 試思此時即不專為穆宗計，既正名為先帝嗣子，豈有僅封一王貝勒者乎？

translations.literal: Consider: even if one did not act solely for Muzong's sake, once he is properly named the late emperor's heir, could he be granted only the title of prince or beile?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting aside concern for Tongzhi alone: once he is formally named heir to the late emperor, could he be given no more than a princely or beile rank?

sentences.zh: 即不專為皇上計，古來天子之嗣子，豈有以不主神器之諸皇子當之者乎？

translations.literal: Even if one did not act solely for the present emperor's sake, in antiquity has a son of Heaven's heir ever been one of the princes not destined to hold the sacred vessel?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting aside concern for the present emperor alone: in all history, has an heir to the Son of Heaven ever been a prince not destined for the throne?

sentences.zh: 即僅為穆宗計，皇上可如民間出繼之子乎？

translations.literal: Even if one acted only for Muzong's sake, could the present emperor be like a common adopted-out son?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one cared only for Tongzhi: could the present emperor be treated like an ordinary adopted-out son?

sentences.zh: 即僅為皇上計，穆宗可如前明稱為皇伯考乎？

translations.literal: Even if one acted only for the present emperor's sake, could Muzong be styled Imperial Uncle, as in the Ming?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one cared only for the present emperor: could Tongzhi be styled Imperial Uncle, as in the Ming dynasty?

sentences.zh: 夫奉祖訓，禀懿旨，體聖意，非僭。

translations.literal: To follow ancestral instruction, receive the empress dowager's decree, and embody the sage emperor's intent is not presumption.
translations.idiomatic: To follow ancestral teaching, heed the empress dowager's decree, and embody the sovereign's intent is not overreaching.

sentences.zh: 先帝今上皆無不宜，非悖。

translations.literal: Neither the late emperor nor the present sovereign is wronged; it is not disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the late emperor nor the present sovereign is slighted; it is not disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 明其統而非其人，非擅。

translations.literal: To clarify the succession line rather than the person is not usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: To clarify the line of succession rather than name a particular person is not usurpation.

sentences.zh: 論統系，辨宗法，正足見國家億萬年無疆之庥，非干犯忌諱。

translations.literal: To discuss the succession system and distinguish clan law is precisely to show the state's blessing of boundless myriad years—it is not to transgress taboo.
translations.idiomatic: To discuss the succession and clarify clan law is precisely to affirm the dynasty's blessing of endless duration—it is not to violate taboo.

sentences.zh: 此固無意氣可逞，亦無功罪可言也。」

translations.literal: Here there is no personal passion to vent, nor merit or fault to be weighed."
translations.idiomatic: This is neither a matter for personal passion nor for claims of merit or blame."

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔存毓慶宮。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered it preserved in the Yuqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered it filed in the Yuqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 自是劾尚書賀壽慈飾奏，俄使崇厚誤國，洪鈞譯地圖舛謬，美使崔國英赴賽會失體，皆人所難言，直聲震中外。

translations.literal: From then on he impeached Minister He Shouci for embellishing memorials, the Russian envoy Chonghou for harming the state, Hong Jun for errors in translating maps, and the American envoy Cui Guoying for impropriety at an exposition—all matters others found hard to speak of—and his upright reputation shook court and foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he denounced Minister He Shouci for falsifying reports, the Russian envoy Chonghou for betraying the nation, Hong Jun for errors in map translation, and the American minister Cui Guoying for misconduct at an exhibition—charges others dared not voice—and his reputation for blunt integrity resounded at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷內閣學士，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Grand Secretary and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 中法事起，建索還琉球、經畫越南議。

translations.literal: When the Sino-French conflict arose, he proposed recovering Ryukyu and planning policy on Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French War broke out, he urged recovery of the Ryukyu kingdom and a comprehensive policy on Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 十一年，還京，劾李鴻章治兵無效，請敕曾紀澤遄歸練師，忤旨，左遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he returned to the capital, impeached Li Hongzhang for ineffective military administration, and requested an order for Zeng Jize to return swiftly and train troops; he offended the throne and was demoted to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he returned to Beijing, attacked Li Hongzhang's failure as commander, and urged that Zeng Jize be recalled at once to train forces; the memorial displeased the court and he was demoted to Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 兩署左副都御史，奏言自強之本在內治，又歷陳中外交涉得失，後卒如所言。

translations.literal: Twice he acted as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; he memorialized that the root of self-strengthening lies in internal governance, and again set forth in detail the gains and losses of Sino-foreign dealings—events later proved him right.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, arguing that self-strengthening must begin at home and detailing the successes and failures of foreign relations—judgments later borne out by events.

sentences.zh: 十七年，乞休。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year.

sentences.zh: 子紹箕、紹第，並能承家學，而紹箕尤贍雅。

translations.literal: His sons Shaoji and Shaodi both could carry on the family learning, and Shaoji was especially cultivated and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shaoji and Shaodi both inherited the family scholarship, Shaoji being especially accomplished and refined.

sentences.zh: 紹箕，字仲弢。

translations.literal: Shaoji, courtesy name Zhongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoji, whose courtesy name was Zhongtao.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，以編修典試湖北。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi and, as an editor, presided over the provincial examination in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Guangxu 6 and, as a Hanlin editor, served as chief examiner for Hubei's provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 晉侍講，擢庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Lecturer and then elevated to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Lecturer and was appointed Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 京師立大學堂，充總辦。

translations.literal: When the Imperial University was established in the capital, he served as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial University was founded in Beijing, he served as its chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 究心東西邦學制，手訂章條。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to Eastern and Western school systems and personally drafted the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Eastern and Western educational systems in depth and personally drafted the university's statutes.

sentences.zh: 遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷充編書局、譯書局監督。

translations.literal: He successively served as supervisor of the Compilation Bureau and the Translation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as supervisor of the Compilation Bureau and the Translation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為湖北提學使。

translations.literal: He went out as educational intendant of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed educational intendant of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 東渡日本，與其邦人士論孔教、輒心折。

translations.literal: He crossed east to Japan and, whenever he debated Confucian teaching with men of that country, they were invariably won over.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling to Japan, he debated Confucian doctrine with Japanese scholars and invariably won their admiration.

sentences.zh: 歸，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: After his return he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after his return he died.

sentences.zh: 宗室寶廷，字竹坡，隸滿洲鑲藍旗，鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗八世孫。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Baoting, courtesy name Zhupo, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was eighth-generation descendant of Prince Xian of Zheng, Jirhalang.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Baoting, whose courtesy name was Zhupo, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was an eighth-generation descendant of Prince Xian of Zheng, Jirhalang.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed an editor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 7, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed editor.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to Lecturer of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，疏請選師保以崇聖德，嚴宦寺以杜干預，覈實內務府以節糜費，訓練神機營以備緩急，懿旨嘉納。

translations.literal: At the change to Guangxu he memorialized requesting selection of tutors to exalt sagely virtue, strict control of eunuchs to block interference, verification of the Imperial Household Department to curtail waste, and training of the Shenji Camp for emergencies; the empress dowager's decree commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangxu he memorialized for the appointment of tutors to cultivate the emperor's virtue, tighter control of eunuchs to prevent interference, audit of the Imperial Household Department to cut waste, and drill of the Shenji Camp for emergencies—all measures praised and accepted by the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 大考三等，降中允，尋授司業。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he received third grade, was demoted to Junior Mentor, and soon after was appointed Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Rated third class in the triennial examination, he was demoted to Junior Mentor and soon appointed Vice Director of Studies.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方銳意求治，詔詢吏治民生用人行政，寶廷力抉其弊，諤諤數百言，至切直。

translations.literal: At this time the court was keen to seek good governance and issued an edict inquiring into official conduct, people's livelihood, appointment of men, and administration; Baoting forcefully exposed its ills in several hundred forthright words, most incisive and direct.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then intent on reform and solicited views on administration, livelihood, appointments, and policy; Baoting exposed abuses in a memorial of several hundred blunt, penetrating words.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，應詔陳言，請罪己，並責臣工。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine, he responded to the edict with memorials requesting self-reproach by the throne and rebuke of officials as well.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan he answered the imperial call for advice, urging the emperor to reproach himself and hold his ministers accountable.

sentences.zh: 條上救荒四事，曰：察釐稅，開糧捐，購洋米，增糶局。

translations.literal: He itemized four measures for famine relief: investigate tax levies, open grain contributions, purchase foreign rice, and increase government grain-sale stations.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed four relief measures: audit tax collection, open grain-donation drives, purchase foreign rice, and expand government grain-sale offices.

sentences.zh: 復以災廣賑劇，請行分貸法。

translations.literal: Again, because the disaster was widespread and relief severe, he requested implementation of a graded-loan method.
translations.idiomatic: Because the disaster was widespread and relief burdens heavy, he also urged a system of graded loans to the afflicted.

sentences.zh: 畿輔旱，日色赤，市言訛駴，建議內嚴防範，外示鎮定，以安人心。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered drought and the sun appeared red, rumors and panic spread in the markets; he proposed strict precautions within and a show of calm without to settle people's minds.
translations.idiomatic: During drought around the capital, when the sun appeared red and rumors panicked the markets, he urged tight internal security and outward calm to steady public sentiment.

sentences.zh: 歷遷侍講學士，以六事進，曰：明黜陟，專責任，詳考詢，嚴程限，去欺矇，慎赦宥，稱旨。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and advanced six proposals: clarify promotion and demotion, fix responsibility, conduct detailed inquiry, enforce strict deadlines, remove deception, and be cautious with amnesties—winning imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting, he submitted six reforms: clarify promotions and demotions, fix responsibility, conduct thorough inquiries, enforce deadlines, root out fraud, and use amnesties sparingly—proposals the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗繼統嗣文宗，懿旨謂將來生有皇子，即繼穆宗為嗣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne as heir to Emperor Wenzong, an empress dowager's decree stated that when a son should be born in future, he would succeed Emperor Muzong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu had first succeeded as heir to Emperor Xianfeng, an empress dowager's decree held that any son born to him in future would succeed Emperor Tongzhi as heir.

sentences.zh: 內閣侍讀學士廣安請頒鐵券，被訶責。

translations.literal: Guang'an, Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Grand Secretariat, requested issuance of an iron certificate and was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'an, Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Grand Secretariat, had asked for an iron bond of assurance and was reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 至是，穆宗奉安惠陵，主事吳可讀堅請為其立後，以屍諫，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: At this point, when Muzong was laid to rest at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup firmly requested that an heir be established for him and remonstrated with his corpse; the court ordered the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Now, when Emperor Tongzhi was interred at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup insisted that an heir be named for him and killed himself in protest; the court ordered a ministerial debate.

sentences.zh: 寶廷謂：「恭繹懿旨之意，蓋言穆宗未有儲貳，即以皇上所生之子為嗣，非言生皇子即時承繼也，言嗣而統賅焉矣。

translations.literal: Baoting said: "Reverently interpreting the empress dowager's decree, it means that since Muzong had no heir apparent, the son born to the present emperor would be his heir—not that a son born would immediately succeed, but that in speaking of heir the succession line is included.
translations.idiomatic: Baoting wrote: "Reverently construed, the empress dowager's decree means that because Tongzhi left no heir, the son the present emperor bears shall be his successor—not that any newborn son must succeed at once, but that 'heir' here embraces the whole line of succession.

sentences.zh: 引伸之，蓋言將來即以皇上傳統之皇子繼穆宗為嗣也。

translations.literal: Extended further, it means that in future the son who inherits the present emperor's line will succeed Muzong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Taken further, it means that in future the son who inherits the present emperor's own line will succeed Tongzhi as heir.

sentences.zh: 因皇上甫承大統，故渾涵其詞，留待親政日自下明詔，此皇太后不忍歧視之慈心，欲以孝弟仁讓之休歸之皇上也。

translations.literal: Because the emperor had only just assumed the great succession, the wording was deliberately broad, to await the day of personal rule when a clear edict would be issued—this is the empress dowager's compassionate heart unwilling to discriminate, wishing to bestow the honor of filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and yielding upon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor had only just ascended the throne, the wording was deliberately broad, leaving a clear edict for the day he took personal rule—this was the empress dowager's compassion, unwilling to divide loyalties, wishing to leave the emperor the credit of filial devotion, brotherly duty, benevolence, and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 廣安不能喻，故生爭於前；

translations.literal: Guang'an could not understand, and therefore contended while alive;
translations.idiomatic: Guang'an failed to grasp this and argued in life;

sentences.zh: 吳可讀不能喻，故死爭於後。

translations.literal: Wu Kedup could not understand, and therefore contended in death afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedup failed to grasp it and contended in death.

sentences.zh: 竊痛可讀殉死之忠，而又惜其遺摺之言不盡意也。

translations.literal: I deeply grieve Kedup's loyal death, yet regret that the words of his final memorial did not fully express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply honor Wu Kedup's loyal sacrifice, yet regret that his final memorial did not fully express his intent.

sentences.zh: 可讀未喻懿旨言外之意，而其遺摺未達之意，皇太后早鑑及之，故曰'前降旨時即是此意'也。

translations.literal: Kedup did not grasp the meaning beyond the empress dowager's decree, yet the meaning his final memorial failed to reach the empress dowager had long discerned, and therefore she said, 'When the earlier edict was issued, it was exactly this meaning.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedup did not grasp what lay beyond the empress dowager's words, yet she had long seen what his memorial left unsaid—hence her declaration that the earlier edict had meant exactly this.

sentences.zh: 而可讀猶以忠佞不齊為慮，誠過慮也。

translations.literal: Yet Kedup still worried that loyal and treacherous ministers would not stand together—truly excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu Kedup still feared that loyal and treacherous ministers would not act as one—a needless anxiety.

sentences.zh: 宋太宗背杜太后，明景帝廢太子見深，雖因佞臣妄進邪說，究由二君有自私之心。

translations.literal: Song Taizong betrayed Empress Dowager Du; Ming Jingdi deposed the heir apparent Zhu Jianshen—though wicked ministers advanced perverse counsel, in the end both rulers harbored selfish hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Song Taizong betrayed Empress Dowager Du's charge; Ming Jingdi deposed the heir Zhu Jianshen—though flatterers fed them false counsel, both rulers acted from selfish motives.

sentences.zh: 乃者兩宮懿旨懸於上，孤臣遺疏存於下，傳之九州，載之國史，皇上天生聖人，必能以皇太后之心為心。

translations.literal: Now the two palaces' decrees hang above and the lone subject's final memorial remains below, to be transmitted through the nine regions and recorded in the national history; the emperor, a sage by nature, will surely take the empress dowager's heart as his own heart.
translations.idiomatic: Now the two palaces' decrees stand above and a lone minister's dying memorial below, to be proclaimed throughout the realm and written into the dynastic record; the emperor, a sage by nature, will surely make the empress dowager's intent his own.

sentences.zh: 請將前後懿旨恭呈御覽，明降諭旨，宣示中外，俾天下後世咸知我皇太后至慈，皇上至孝至弟至仁至讓，且以見穆宗至聖至明，付託得人也。

translations.literal: I request that the earlier and later empress dowager decrees be respectfully presented for imperial review, that a clear edict be issued and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all under heaven and posterity may know our empress dowager's utmost compassion, the emperor's utmost filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and yielding, and may also see Muzong's utmost sagacity and clarity in entrusting the right man.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the earlier and later decrees be presented for the emperor's review, that a clear edict be issued and proclaimed at home and abroad, so that all the world and posterity may know the empress dowager's boundless compassion, the emperor's supreme filial piety, brotherly duty, benevolence, and forbearance—and may see that Tongzhi, most sage and discerning, entrusted his line to the right man.

sentences.zh: 如是，則綱紀正，名分定，天理順，人情安矣。

translations.literal: If so, then moral order is correct, titles are fixed, heavenly principle is followed, and human sentiment is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Then moral order will be restored, titles fixed, heaven's way satisfied, and human hearts at ease.

sentences.zh: 因赴內閣集議，意微不合，謹以上聞。」

translations.literal: Because at the Grand Secretariat assembly my view differed slightly, I respectfully report the above."
translations.idiomatic: Finding my view at slight variance with the Grand Secretariat deliberation, I respectfully submit this for the throne's attention."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「廷臣謂穆宗繼統之議，已賅於皇太后前降懿旨之中，將來神器所歸，皇上自能斟酌盡善，固也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The court ministers say the question of Muzong's succession is already included in the empress dowager's earlier decree, and that when the sacred vessel finds its place in future the emperor himself can weigh all matters to perfection—this is so.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Ministers say the question of Tongzhi's succession is already covered by the empress dowager's earlier decree, and that when the throne passes in future the emperor can weigh every matter to perfection—so far, so good.

sentences.zh: 然懿旨意深詞簡，不及此引伸明晰，異日皇上生有皇子，將繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不即繼乎？

translations.literal: Yet the empress dowager's intent is deep and her words brief; without this extended clarification, when the emperor bears a son in future, will he succeed Muzong as heir, or not succeed immediately?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the decree's intent is deep and its wording brief; without this fuller explanation, when the emperor has a son, will that son succeed Tongzhi at once or not?

sentences.zh: 不即繼似違懿旨，即繼又嫌跡近建儲。

translations.literal: Not succeeding immediately seems to violate the decree; succeeding immediately seems close to designating an heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Not succeeding at once would seem to violate the decree; succeeding at once would look too much like naming a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 就令僅言繼嗣，不標繼統之名，而臣民亦隱以儲貳視之，是不建之建也。

translations.literal: Even if one spoke only of succeeding as heir without labeling succession to the line, officials and people would still tacitly regard him as heir apparent—this is establishing an heir without establishing one.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one spoke only of heirship without naming succession to the line, officials and people would still treat the child as crown prince in all but name—establishing an heir without formally doing so.

sentences.zh: 而此皇子賢也，固宗社福；

translations.literal: If this prince is worthy, it is indeed the fortune of the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: If that prince proves worthy, the realm is blessed;

sentences.zh: 如其不賢，將來仍傳繼統乎，抑舍而別傳乎？

translations.literal: if he is not worthy, in future will the succession line still be transmitted to him, or set aside for another transmission?
translations.idiomatic: if he proves unworthy, will the line still pass to him, or be set aside for another?

sentences.zh: 別傳之皇子，仍繼穆宗為嗣乎，抑不繼乎？

translations.literal: Would the prince of the other transmission still succeed Muzong as heir, or not?
translations.idiomatic: Would a prince from another line still succeed Tongzhi as heir, or not?

sentences.zh: 即使仍繼穆宗，是亦不廢立之廢立也，豈太平盛事乎？

translations.literal: Even if he still succeeded Muzong, this would be deposition and installation without deposition and installation—how could it be an occasion of great peace?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he did succeed Tongzhi, that would amount to deposing and enthroning without calling it so—hardly an age of great peace, would it?

sentences.zh: 至此時即欲皇上斟酌盡善，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: By that time, even if the emperor wished to weigh all to perfection, would it not be difficult?
translations.idiomatic: By then, could the emperor still weigh every matter to perfection?

sentences.zh: 廷議之意，或以皇上親政，皇子應尚未生，不難豫酌一盡善之規。

translations.literal: The intent of the court debate may be that when the emperor takes personal rule the prince will not yet have been born, and it will not be hard to pre-weigh a perfect plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers may think that when the emperor takes personal rule no prince will yet have been born, making it easy to frame a perfect plan in advance.

sentences.zh: 然國君十五而生子，皇子誕育如在徹簾之前，又何以處之乎？

translations.literal: Yet rulers at fifteen bear sons; if a prince is born before the curtain of regency is drawn, how is one to handle it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet rulers commonly father sons at fifteen; if a prince is born before the regency ends, what then?

sentences.zh: 與其留此兩難之局以待皇上，何如及今斟酌盡善乎？

translations.literal: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, would it not be better to weigh all to perfection now?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than leave this dilemma for the emperor, would it not be better to settle it now?

sentences.zh: 且懿旨非皇上可改，此時不引伸明晰，將來皇上雖斟酌盡善，何敢自為變通乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, the empress dowager's decree is not something the emperor may alter; if it is not extended and clarified now, in future even if the emperor wished to weigh all to perfection, how would he dare change it on his own?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the empress dowager's decree is not the emperor's to alter; if it is not clarified now, how could he later dare change it even if he wished to?

sentences.zh: 此未妥者一也。

translations.literal: This is one point not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first flaw in the ministers' plan.

sentences.zh: 廷議又謂繼統與建儲，文義似殊，而事體則一，似也。

translations.literal: The court debate also says that succeeding to the line and establishing an heir apparent differ in wording yet are one in substance—this seems so.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers also say that succession to the line and naming a crown prince differ in wording but not in substance—so it seems.

sentences.zh: 然列聖垂訓，原言嗣統之常，今則事屬創局，可讀意在存穆宗之統，與無故擅請建儲者有間，文義之殊，不待言矣。

translations.literal: Yet the instructions left by successive sage emperors spoke of the regular rule of heir and succession; today's matter is an unprecedented situation. Kedup's intent was to preserve Muzong's line, distinct from those who without cause presumptuously request establishment of an heir—the difference in wording needs no elaboration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the teaching of our sage forebears concerned the normal rule of heir and succession; today's case is unprecedented. Wu Kedup sought to preserve Tongzhi's line—quite unlike those who presumptuously demand a crown prince without cause. The difference in wording scarcely needs stating.

sentences.zh: 今廷議不分別詞意，漫謂我朝家法未能深知，則日前懿旨'即是此意'之謂何，臣民不更滋疑乎？

translations.literal: Now the court debate does not distinguish the terms and casually says our dynasty's household law is not deeply understood—then what of the empress dowager's earlier words 'exactly this meaning'? Will not officials and people only grow more doubtful?
translations.idiomatic: If ministers refuse to distinguish the terms and casually claim ignorance of dynastic law, what becomes of the empress dowager's words 'exactly this meaning'? Will not officials and people only grow more suspicious?

sentences.zh: 此未妥者又一也。」

translations.literal: This is another point not yet settled."
translations.idiomatic: This is the second flaw."

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔藏毓慶宮。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered it stored in the Yuqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered it filed in the Yuqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 其他，俄使來議約，朝鮮請通商，均有所獻納。

translations.literal: On other matters, when the Russian envoy came to negotiate a treaty and Korea requested trade, he offered proposals on each.
translations.idiomatic: On other matters too—Russian treaty negotiations, Korea's request for trade—he submitted thoughtful proposals.

sentences.zh: 七年，授內閣學士，出典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary and went out to preside over the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary and sent to preside over Fujian's provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 既蕆事，還朝，以在途納妾自劾罷，築室西山，往居之。

translations.literal: When the assignment was completed, he returned to court, impeached himself and was dismissed for taking a concubine on the journey, built a house on the Western Hills, and went to live there.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his duties he returned to the capital, resigned in self-accusation for taking a concubine en route, built a residence on the Western Hills, and retired there.

sentences.zh: 是冬，皇太后萬壽祝嘏，賞三品秩。

translations.literal: That winter, for the empress dowager's longevity birthday felicitations, he was granted third-rank standing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the empress dowager's birthday celebrations, he was honored with third-rank standing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子壽富，庶吉士。

translations.literal: His son Shoufu was a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoufu served as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 庚子，拳匪亂，殉難，自有傳。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, during the Boxer uprising, he died a martyr's death; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year of the Boxer Rebellion he died a martyr's death; his life is recorded in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宗室盛昱，字伯熙，隸滿洲鑲白旗，肅武親王豪格七世孫。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Sheng Yu, courtesy name Boxi, belonged to the Manchu Bordered White Banner and was seventh-generation descendant of Prince Suwu, Hooge.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Sheng Yu, whose courtesy name was Boxi, belonged to the Manchu Bordered White Banner and was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Suwu, Hooge.

sentences.zh: 祖敬徵，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingzheng was Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingzheng had served as Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 父恆恩，左副都御史。

translations.literal: His father Heng'en was Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heng'en had been Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 盛昱少慧，十歲時作詩用「特勤」字，據唐闕特勤碑證新唐書突厥「純特勒」為「特勤」之誤，繇是顯名。

translations.literal: Sheng Yu was clever in youth; at ten he used the character teqin in a poem and, citing the Tang stele of Kül Tigin, proved that the New Tang History's Turkic chun tele was an error for teqin, and thereby won fame.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yu showed exceptional talent as a boy. At ten he used the term teqin in a poem and, citing the Tang stele of Kül Tigin, demonstrated that the New Tang History's Turkic chun tele was a misreading of teqin—an achievement that brought him wide renown.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，既，授編修，益厲學，討測經史、輿地及本朝掌故，皆能詳其沿革。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he became a jinshi; thereafter he was appointed an editor, applied himself more vigorously to study, and investigated classics, history, geography, and institutions of the present dynasty, all of which he could trace in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Guangxu 2 and was appointed a Hanlin editor. He redoubled his studies, researching the classics, history, geography, and Qing institutional precedents until he could narrate their evolution in full detail.

sentences.zh: 累遷右庶子，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Right Junior Tutor and served as an official of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to Right Junior Tutor and was appointed to the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督何璟、巡撫劉秉璋收降台匪黃金滿，盛昱劾璟等長惡養奸，請下吏嚴議，發金滿黑龍江、新疆安置。

translations.literal: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General He Jing and Governor Liu Bingzhang accepted the surrender of the Taiwan bandit Huang Jinman; Sheng Yu impeached Jing and others for indulging evil and nurturing treachery, requested that they be referred to the judiciary for strict deliberation, and that Jinman be sent to Heilongjiang and Xinjiang for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General He Jing and Governor Liu Bingzhang accepted the surrender of the Taiwan rebel Huang Jinman, Sheng Yu attacked them for sheltering criminals and urged strict judicial review, with Jinman exiled to Heilongjiang and Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 尚書彭玉麟數辭官不受職，劾其自便身圖，啟功臣驕蹇之漸。

translations.literal: Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly declined office and would not accept appointment; he impeached him for scheming personal convenience and opening the way for meritorious ministers' arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly refused office, Sheng Yu impeached him for putting personal ease first and encouraging the arrogance of meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 浙江按察使陳寶箴陛見未行，追論官河南聽獄不慎，罷免；

translations.literal: Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Chen Baozhen had not yet departed for his audience with the throne when Sheng Yu pursued the matter of his careless adjudication while serving in Henan, and he was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Chen Baozhen could depart for his audience with the throne, Sheng Yu revived charges of careless adjudication from Chen's tenure in Henan, and Chen was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 張佩綸劾其留京幹進，寶箴疏辯，盛昱言其嘵嘵失大臣體，請再下吏議。

translations.literal: Zhang Peilun impeached him for remaining in the capital to seek advancement; Baozhen memorialized in defense, and Sheng Yu said his clamor lacked the bearing of a great minister and requested that he again be referred to the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peilun then charged him with lingering in Beijing to lobby for promotion. When Chen Baozhen defended himself in a memorial, Sheng Yu declared that his noisy self-defense was unbecoming a senior minister and urged another referral to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮之亂也，提督吳長慶奉北洋大臣張樹聲檄，率師入朝，執大院君李罡應以歸，時詫為奇勳。

translations.literal: During the Korean disturbance, Commander Wu Changqing, on orders from Beiyang Commissioner Zhang Shusheng, led troops into Korea and seized the Taewon-gun Li Gang-yeo and brought him back—a deed then hailed as a singular exploit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Korean crisis, Commander Wu Changqing, acting on orders from Beiyang Commissioner Zhang Shusheng, marched into Korea, seized the Taewon-gun Li Gang-yeo, and brought him back—an exploit then widely praised as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 盛昱言：「出自誘劫，不足言功，徒令屬國寒心，友邦騰笑。

translations.literal: Sheng Yu said: "It arose from enticement and abduction and is not worth calling merit; it only makes the tributary state lose heart and friendly states burst into laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yu wrote: "This arose from entrapment and abduction and cannot be called merit; it only chills our tributary ally and invites ridicule abroad.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴予處分，俾中外知非朝廷本意。」

translations.literal: They should be sternly punished, so that within and without all may know this was not the court's intent."
translations.idiomatic: They should be sternly punished, so that at home and abroad all may know this was never the court's intent."

sentences.zh: 為講官未半載，數言事，士論推為謇諤。

translations.literal: He had been a lecturer for less than half a year yet repeatedly spoke on affairs of state, and scholarly opinion esteemed him as bluntly remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had served as lecturer for less than half a year, he repeatedly memorialized on state affairs, and public opinion hailed him as a fearless remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷祭酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 法越構釁，徐延旭'唐炯坐失地逮問，盛昱言：「逮問疆臣而不明降諭旨，二百年來無此政體。」

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam came into conflict, Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong were arrested and questioned for losing territory; Sheng Yu said: "To arrest and question frontier ministers without issuing a clear imperial edict—in two hundred years there has been no such form of government."
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict erupted, Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong were arrested for losing territory. Sheng Yu wrote: "To seize and interrogate frontier officials without a clear imperial edict—in two hundred years there has been no precedent for such a procedure."

sentences.zh: 並劾樞臣怠職。

translations.literal: He also impeached the Grand Council ministers for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached the Grand Council ministers for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，罷恭親王奕訢等，而詔醇親王奕枻入樞府，盛昱復言：「醇親王分地綦崇，不宜嬰以政務。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and dismissed Prince Gong Yixin and others, but decreed that Prince Chun Yixuan enter the Grand Council; Sheng Yu again said: "Prince Chun's princely rank is exceedingly exalted and he should not be burdened with administrative affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was enraged and dismissed Prince Gong Yixin and others, but then summoned Prince Chun Yixuan to the Grand Council. Sheng Yu protested again: "Prince Chun's princely station is too exalted to be burdened with routine state affairs."

sentences.zh: 其夏，命廷臣會議和戰大局，盛昱主速戰，力陳七利，謂：「再失事機，噬臍無及。」

translations.literal: That summer the court ordered ministers to confer on the overall question of peace or war; Sheng Yu advocated swift war, forcefully set forth seven advantages, and said: "If the opportunity is lost again, there will be no remedy but to bite one's navel in regret."
translations.idiomatic: That summer the court ordered a ministerial debate on war and peace. Sheng Yu argued for immediate war, setting forth seven advantages and warning: "If we miss our chance again, we shall bite our navels in vain regret."

sentences.zh: 盛昱為祭酒，與司業治麟究心教士之法，大治學舍，加膏火，定積分日程，懲遊惰，獎樸學，士習為之一變。

translations.literal: As chancellor, Sheng Yu together with Vice Director Zhi Lin devoted themselves to methods of instructing scholars, greatly renovated the academy buildings, increased stipends, fixed a schedule of cumulative points, punished idleness, rewarded solid learning, and student conduct was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Sheng Yu and Vice Director Zhi Lin overhauled instruction at the academy: they renovated the dormitories, increased stipends, instituted a points-based schedule, punished idleness, rewarded serious scholarship—and student conduct was transformed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，典試山東。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he served as chief examiner for Shandong's provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: The next year he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 盛昱家居有清譽，承學之士以得接言論風采為幸。

translations.literal: Sheng Yu at home enjoyed a reputation for integrity, and scholars who inherited the tradition counted it good fortune to meet his discourse and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement Sheng Yu enjoyed a reputation for integrity, and young scholars considered it a privilege to hear him speak and observe his manner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fifth year.

sentences.zh: 張佩綸，字幼樵，直隸豐潤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Peilun, courtesy name Youqiao, was a man of Fengrun in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Peilun, whose courtesy name was Youqiao, came from Fengrun in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父印塘，官安徽按察使，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His father Yintang served as Anhui Surveillance Commissioner and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yintang had served as Anhui Surveillance Commissioner and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 佩綸，成同治十年進士，以編脩大考擢侍講，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: Peilun became a jinshi in the tenth year of Tongzhi; through the grand examination as an editor he was elevated to Lecturer and served as an official of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 10; rated highly in the triennial examination as a Hanlin editor, he was promoted to Lecturer and appointed to the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 時外侮亟，累疏陳經國大政，請敕新疆、東三省、台灣嚴戒備，杜日、俄窺伺。

translations.literal: At the time foreign aggression was pressing; he repeatedly memorialized on great policies for ordering the state, requesting orders for strict defense of Xinjiang, the three eastern provinces, and Taiwan to block Japanese and Russian covetous observation.
translations.idiomatic: As foreign pressure mounted, he repeatedly memorialized on fundamental state policy, urging strict defenses for Xinjiang, the Northeast, and Taiwan to forestall Japanese and Russian encroachment.

sentences.zh: 晉、豫飢，畿輔旱，乃引祖宗成訓，請上下交儆，條四目以進：曰誠祈，曰集議，曰恤民，曰省刑。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered famine and the capital region drought, he cited ancestral precedents and requested mutual vigilance above and below, submitting four items: sincere prayer, collective deliberation, relief of the people, and reduction of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shanxi and Henan and drought around the capital, he cited ancestral teaching and urged vigilance at every level, proposing four measures: sincere prayer, collective deliberation, relief for the people, and reduction of punishments.

sentences.zh: 恭親王奕訢遭讒構，復請責王竭誠負重，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Prince Gong Yixin suffered slanderous plotting, he again requested that the prince be charged to serve with full devotion and heavy responsibility; the throne commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gong Yixin fell victim to slander, Peilun urged that the prince be entrusted with full authority and devotion—a proposal the emperor praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 通政使黃體芳繼陳災狀，語稍激，絓吏議，佩綸力爭，被宥。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Transmission Huang Tifang next reported disaster conditions in somewhat heated language and was caught in official censure; Peilun argued forcefully and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Commissioner of Transmission Huang Tifang next reported on disasters in heated language and faced disciplinary action, Peilun argued vigorously on his behalf and Huang was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂，服竟，起故官。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended, he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時琉球已亡，法圖越南亟，佩綸曰：「亡琉球則朝鮮可危，棄越南則緬甸必失。」

translations.literal: At the time Ryukyu had perished and France was pressing on Vietnam; Peilun said: "If Ryukyu is lost, Korea will be in peril; if Vietnam is abandoned, Burma will surely be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu had already fallen and France was pressing hard on Vietnam. Peilun warned: "Lose Ryukyu and Korea is endangered; abandon Vietnam and Burma will surely follow."

sentences.zh: 因請建置南北海防，設水師四大鎮；

translations.literal: He therefore requested establishment of northern and southern coastal defense and four major naval commands;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged coastal defenses north and south and four major naval commands;

sentences.zh: 又薦道員徐延旭、唐炯知兵堪任邊事，其招致劉永福黑旗兵為己用。

translations.literal: he also recommended Circuit Intendants Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong as knowing warfare and fit for frontier affairs, and that they recruit Liu Yongfu's Black Flag troops for their own use.
translations.idiomatic: he also recommended Circuit Intendants Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong as military men fit for frontier duty, and urged them to enlist Liu Yongfu's Black Flag Army for their own forces.

sentences.zh: 是時吳大澂、陳寶琛好論時政，與寶廷、鄧承修輩號「清流黨」，而佩綸尤以糾彈大臣著一時。

translations.literal: At this time Wu Dacheng and Chen Baochen liked to discuss current policy; together with Baoting, Deng Chengxiu, and others they were called the Qingliu Party, while Peilun was especially noted in his time for impeaching great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wu Dacheng and Chen Baochen were outspoken on current affairs; with Baoting, Deng Chengxiu, and others they were known as the Qingliu Party, while Peilun was especially famed for impeaching senior officials.

sentences.zh: 如侍郎賀壽慈，尚書萬青藜、董恂，皆被劾去。

translations.literal: Such as Vice Ministers He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun—all were impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun were among those he drove from office.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，雲南報銷案起，王文韶以樞臣掌戶部，臺諫爭上其受賕狀，上方意任隆密，乃援乾隆朝梁詩正還家侍父事，請令引嫌乞養，不報；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu the Yunnan reimbursement case arose; Wang Wenshao, as a Grand Council minister, headed the Board of Revenue, and censors and remonstrators competed to report his taking bribes; the throne still trusted him deeply, so Peilun cited the Qianlong case of Liang Shizheng returning home to serve his father and requested that Wang withdraw on grounds of conflict and beg to retire, but received no reply;
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 the Yunnan reimbursement scandal broke. Wang Wenshao, a Grand Council minister, also headed the Board of Revenue, and censors flooded the court with charges of bribery. Though the emperor still trusted him, Peilun cited the Qianlong precedent of Liang Shizheng retiring to care for his father and urged Wang to withdraw on grounds of conflict—without response;

sentences.zh: 又兩疏劾之，遂罷文韶，而擢佩緰署左副都御史，晉侍講學士。

translations.literal: he memorialized twice more to impeach him, and Wenshao was dismissed; Peilun was elevated to act as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: after two further impeachment memorials Wang was dismissed, and Peilun was appointed acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 明年，法越構釁，佩綸章十數上，朝廷始遣兵徵土寇、綴敵勢，法人不便其所，佯議和，而陰使人攻陷南定。

translations.literal: The next year, when France and Vietnam came into conflict, Peilun submitted more than a dozen memorials; the court then sent troops to suppress local bandits and check the enemy, but the French found this inconvenient, feigned peace talks, and secretly had men capture Nanding.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the Sino-French conflict erupted, Peilun submitted more than a dozen memorials. The court finally sent troops against local bandits to check the French advance, but the French, finding this inconvenient, feigned peace talks while secretly capturing Nanding.

sentences.zh: 佩綸請乘法兵未集，敕粵督遣水越都，而樞臣狃和局，慮佩綸梗議，令往陝西按事。

translations.literal: Peilun requested that while French troops were not yet assembled, the Guangdong governor be ordered to send naval forces to the Vietnamese capital, but the Grand Council clung to peace and, fearing Peilun would obstruct deliberations, ordered him to Shaanxi to investigate a case.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun urged striking before French forces concentrated and ordering the Guangdong governor to send a fleet to the Vietnamese capital. The Grand Council, clinging to peace and fearing Peilun would block their deliberations, sent him to Shaanxi on an investigation.

sentences.zh: 已而法果襲順化，脅越與盟，越事益壞。

translations.literal: Before long the French indeed attacked Hue, coerced Vietnam into alliance, and the Vietnamese situation grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the French attacked Hue, forced Vietnam into alliance, and the Vietnamese situation deteriorated further.

sentences.zh: 使歸，命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, he was ordered to serve at the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was assigned to the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，法人聲內犯，佩綸謂越難未已，黑旗猶存，萬無分兵東來理，請毋罷戍啟戎心，上韙之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the French threatened invasion inland; Peilun said the Vietnamese crisis was not over, the Black Flags still survived, and there was absolutely no reason to divide forces and come east, and requested that garrisons not be withdrawn lest warlike intent be aroused; the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the French threatened coastal invasion, Peilun argued that the Vietnamese crisis was unresolved, the Black Flags still held the field, and France had no reason to divert forces eastward. He urged that garrisons not be withdrawn lest war be provoked—the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔就李鴻章議，遂決戰，令以三品卿銜會辦福建海疆事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered consultation with Li Hongzhang, war was decided, and he was ordered to assist in Fujian maritime affairs with the rank of third-grade commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court consulted Li Hongzhang and decided on war, appointing Peilun third-grade commissioner to oversee Fujian's coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 佩綸至船廠，環十一艘自衛，各管帶白非計，斥之。

translations.literal: Peilun arrived at the naval yard and surrounded himself with eleven vessels for self-defense; the various commanders explained it was no plan of theirs, and he rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Foochow Navy Yard Peilun surrounded himself with eleven vessels for protection. When the commanders protested that this was no plan of theirs, he rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 法艦集，戰書至，眾聞警，謁佩綸亟請備，仍叱出。

translations.literal: French warships gathered, a challenge arrived, and when all heard the alarm they visited Peilun urgently requesting preparations, but he still drove them out with rebukes.
translations.idiomatic: When French warships gathered and a challenge arrived, his officers rushed to urge preparations; he drove them out with rebukes.

sentences.zh: 比見法艦升火，始大怖，遣學生魏瀚往乞緩，未至而砲聲作，所部五營潰，其三營殲焉。

translations.literal: Only when he saw the French ships raise steam did he become greatly terrified; he sent student Wei Han to beg a respite, but before he arrived cannon fire began, his five battalions routed, and three of them were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he saw the French ships raising steam did panic set in. He sent student Wei Han to beg for a truce, but before Wei arrived the guns opened fire; five battalions routed, three of them annihilated.

sentences.zh: 佩綸遁鼓山麓，鄉人拒之，曰：「我會辦大臣也！」

translations.literal: Peilun fled to the foot of Mount Gu, and the villagers refused him, saying: "I am the commissioner in charge!"
translations.idiomatic: Peilun fled toward Mount Gu, but villagers turned him away. He cried: "I am the commissioner in charge!"

sentences.zh: 拒如初。

translations.literal: They refused him as before.
translations.idiomatic: They refused him just the same.

sentences.zh: 翼日，逃至彭田鄉，猶飾詞入告，朝旨發帑犒之，命兼船政。

translations.literal: The next day he fled to Pengtian village, still embellishing his words in reports; the court ordered treasury funds to reward him and appointed him concurrently Superintendent of the Naval Yard.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fled to Pengtian village, still filing embellished reports. The court ordered treasury funds to reward him and appointed him concurrent Superintendent of the Naval Yard.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞馬尾敗，止奪卿銜，下吏議。

translations.literal: When word came of the Mawei defeat, he was only stripped of his commissioner rank and referred to the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the Mawei disaster arrived, he was merely stripped of his commissioner rank and referred to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 閩人憤甚，於是編修潘炳年、給事中萬培因等先後上其罪狀。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian were greatly enraged; thereupon Editor Pan Bingnian, Censor Wan Peiyin, and others successively reported his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was outraged. Editor Pan Bingnian, Censor Wan Peiyin, and others then filed memorial after memorial detailing his offenses.

sentences.zh: 時已坐薦唐尚、徐延旭褫職，至是再論戍。

translations.literal: He had already been punished for recommending Tang Shang and Xu Yanxu with dismissal from office; now he was again sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been dismissed for recommending Tang Shang and Xu Yanxu; now he was sentenced to exile again.

sentences.zh: 居邊釋還，鴻章再延入幕，以女妻之。

translations.literal: After living in exile he was released and returned; Hongzhang again invited him into his staff and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After his exile he was released and Li Hongzhang again took him onto his staff, giving him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 甲什戰事起，御史端良劾其乾預公事，命遂回籍。

translations.literal: When the Jiawu War broke out, Censor Duan Liang impeached him for meddling in public affairs, and he was ordered to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Sino-Japanese War broke out, Censor Duan Liang impeached him for meddling in public affairs, and he was ordered home.

sentences.zh: 庚子議和，鴻章薦其諳交涉，詔以編佐辦和約。

translations.literal: During the gengzi peace negotiations, Hongzhang recommended him as versed in diplomacy, and an edict appointed him as an editor to assist in drafting the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: During the Boxer peace negotiations of 1900, Li Hongzhang recommended him as skilled in diplomacy, and the court appointed him an editor to help draft the treaty.

sentences.zh: 既成，擢四五品京堂，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: When it was completed, he was elevated to fourth- or fifth-rank capital official, but pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the treaty was signed he was promoted to a fourth- or fifth-rank capital post but pleaded illness and declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 何如璋，字子瓘，籍廣東大埔。

translations.literal: He Ruzhang, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in Dapu, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruzhang, whose courtesy name was Zijin, was a native of Dapu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed an editor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 7, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed editor.

sentences.zh: 以侍讀出使日本。

translations.literal: As Reader he was sent as envoy to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: As a Hanlin Reader he was dispatched as envoy to Japan.

sentences.zh: 歸，授少詹事，出督船政。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Junior Vice Director of the Hanlin and went out to superintend the naval yard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Junior Vice Director of the Hanlin and sent to superintend the naval yard.

sentences.zh: 承鴻章旨，狃和議，敵至，猶嚴諭各艦毋妄動。

translations.literal: Following Hongzhang's intent, he clung to peace talks; when the enemy arrived, he still sternly ordered each vessel not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Hongzhang's policy of peace, he clung to negotiation; when the enemy arrived he still sternly ordered every ship not to move.

sentences.zh: 及敗，藉口押銀出奔，所如勿納，不得已，往就佩綸彭田鄉。

translations.literal: When defeat came, he used escorting silver as a pretext to flee; wherever he went he was not admitted, and having no choice he went to join Peilun at Pengtian village.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat he fled on the pretext of escorting funds; nowhere would admit him, and in desperation he sought out Peilun at Pengtian village.

sentences.zh: 佩綸慮敵踪跡及之，紿如璋出。

translations.literal: Peilun feared the enemy's trail would reach him and deceived Ruzhang into leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Peilun, fearing the enemy would track him down, tricked Ruzhang into leaving.

sentences.zh: 士論謂閩事之壞，佩綸為罪魁，如璋次之。

translations.literal: Scholarly opinion held that in the ruin of Fujian affairs, Peilun was the chief culprit and Ruzhang next.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Peilun was chiefly to blame for the Fujian disaster and Ruzhang second.

sentences.zh: 如璋亦遣戍。

translations.literal: Ruzhang was also sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhang was also exiled.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 鄧承修，字鐵香，廣東歸善人。

translations.literal: Deng Chengxiu, courtesy name Tiexiang, was a man of Guishan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chengxiu, whose courtesy name was Tiexiang, came from Guishan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 舉咸豐十一年鄉試，入貲為郎，分刑部。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the eleventh year of Xianfeng, purchased office as a secretary, and was assigned to the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Xianfeng 11, purchased office as a secretary, and was assigned to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 轉御史，遭憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor but returned home on bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to censor but returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, when mourning ended, he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, when his mourning ended, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 與張佩綸等主持清議，多彈擊，號曰「鐵漢」。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Peilun and others he led pure criticism, frequently impeaching, and was called the Iron Han.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Peilun and others he led the Qingliu faction's moral criticism, impeaching officials relentlessly, and was known as the Iron Han.

sentences.zh: 先後疏論闈姓賭捐，大乖政體；

translations.literal: He successively memorialized on surname-based examination gambling contributions, a grave departure from proper government;
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly denounced surname-based examination gambling contributions as a grave corruption of governance;

sentences.zh: 關稅侵蝕，嬰害庫帑；

translations.literal: customs revenue erosion, harming the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: customs revenue embezzlement that drained the treasury;

sentences.zh: 以考場積弊，陳七事糾正之；

translations.literal: on accumulated examination abuses, he set forth seven matters to correct them;
translations.idiomatic: on entrenched examination abuses, he proposed seven reforms;

sentences.zh: 吏治積弊，陳八事肅澄之。

translations.literal: on accumulated official malfeasance, he set forth eight matters to purge and clarify them.
translations.idiomatic: on entrenched official corruption, he proposed eight measures to purge it.

sentences.zh: 又劾總督李瀚章失政，左副都御史崇勳無行，侍郎長敘等違制，學政吳寶恕、葉大焯，布政使方大湜、龔易圖，鹽運使周星譽諸不職狀。

translations.literal: He also impeached Governor Li Hanzhang for maladministration, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Chong Xun for misconduct, Vice Ministers Chang Xu and others for violating regulations, and Educational Commissioners Wu Baoshu and Ye Dachao, Provincial Administration Commissioners Fang Dashen and Gong Yitu, and Salt Controller Zhou Xingyu for various failures in office.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Governor Li Hanzhang for maladministration, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Chong Xun for misconduct, Vice Ministers including Chang Xu for violating regulations, and Educational Commissioners Wu Baoshu and Ye Dachao, Provincial Administration Commissioners Fang Dashen and Gong Yitu, and Salt Controller Zhou Xingyu for various failures in office.

sentences.zh: 會邊警，糾彈舉朝慢弛，請召還左宗棠柄國政。

translations.literal: When frontier alarms arose, he impeached the whole court for laxity and requested recall of Zuo Zongtang to hold state power.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier alarms arose, he attacked the whole court for laxity and urged that Zuo Zongtang be recalled to direct state affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，彗星見，則又言宗棠蒞事數月，未見設施，而因推及寶鋆、王文韶之昏眊，請罷斥，回天意。

translations.literal: After a year a comet appeared; he then said Zongtang had taken office for months without visible measures, and extended this to the dimness of Baojun and Wang Wenshao, requesting dismissal to turn back heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when a comet appeared, he declared that Zuo Zongtang had held office for months without visible achievement, extended his attack to the senility of Baojun and Wang Wenshao, and urged their dismissal to appease heaven.

sentences.zh: 是時文韶方鄉用，權任轉重，會雲南報銷案起，又嚴劾之，仍不允。

translations.literal: At this time Wenshao was being brought into use from the provinces and his power grew heavier; when the Yunnan reimbursement case arose, he again impeached him sternly, but still without approval.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao was then rising from provincial service to greater power. When the Yunnan reimbursement scandal broke, Deng impeached him again—still without success.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷給事中。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時朝鮮亂平，琉球案未結，上言簡知兵大臣駐煙台，厚集南北洋戰艦番巡，留吳長慶軍戍朝互犄角。

translations.literal: At the time the Korean disturbance was settled but the Ryukyu case unresolved; he memorialized to select a minister knowing warfare to station at Yantai, heavily gather Northern and Southern Fleet warships for rotating patrol, and leave Wu Changqing's army garrisoned in Korea in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Korea was pacified but the Ryukyu question remained open. He urged appointing a military minister at Yantai, concentrating Northern and Southern Fleet warships for patrol, and keeping Wu Changqing's army in Korea as a counterweight.

sentences.zh: 越南亂作，法人襲順化，復請詔百官廷議定國是，皆不報。

translations.literal: When the Vietnamese disturbance broke out and the French attacked Hue, he again requested an edict summoning all officials to court deliberation to fix national policy—all without reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Vietnam erupted and the French seized Hue, he again urged a court assembly of all officials to settle national policy—all without response.

sentences.zh: 十年，越事益壞，首劾徐延旭、唐炯失地喪師，趙沃、黃桂蘭擁兵僨事，宜肅國憲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Vietnamese situation grew worse; he was first to impeach Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong for losing territory and armies, and Zhao Wo and Huang Guilan for holding troops and ruining affairs—national law should be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as Vietnam deteriorated, he was first to impeach Xu Yanxu and Tang Jiong for losing territory and armies, and Zhao Wo and Huang Guilan for misusing troops and ruining the campaign—urging that national law be enforced.

sentences.zh: 其夏，法人原媾和，承修聯合臺諫上書，極言和議難恃。

translations.literal: That summer the French wished to negotiate peace; Chengxiu joined censors and remonstrators in memorials, strongly stating that peace talks could not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the French sought peace, Chengxiu joined censors and remonstrators in memorials declaring peace talks untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 旋與司業潘衍桐密上間敵五策，並劾李鴻章定和之疏，嫉劉永福敢戰，言之憤絕。

translations.literal: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems for probing the enemy, and also impeached Li Hongzhang's memorial fixing peace, resenting Liu Yongfu's willingness to fight—he spoke with utmost indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Vice Director Pan Yantong in secretly submitting five stratagems against the enemy and impeached Li Hongzhang's peace memorial, raging with indignation at Li's hostility to Liu Yongfu's fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 亡何，法果敗盟，侵台灣雞籠，樞臣議和戰未決。

translations.literal: Before long the French indeed broke the treaty and invaded Jilong in Taiwan; the Grand Council debated peace and war without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the French broke the treaty and attacked Jilong in Taiwan, while the Grand Council remained undecided between war and peace.

sentences.zh: 於是承修再陳三策：「法所恃為援者西貢、東京。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengxiu again set forth three stratagems: "What the French rely on as support are Saigon and Tonkin.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu then proposed three stratagems: "France's bases of support are Saigon and Tonkin.

sentences.zh: 我若師分三路，亟攻越南，彼將自救不暇，策之上也。

translations.literal: If our armies divide into three routes and swiftly attack Vietnam, they will be too busy saving themselves—this is the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If we divide our forces into three columns and strike Vietnam swiftly, they will be too busy defending themselves to aid Taiwan—the superior stratagem.

sentences.zh: 分兵為守，敵至則戰，敵退不追，老師糜餉，利害共之，策之中也。

translations.literal: Divide troops for defense, fight when the enemy comes, do not pursue when they retreat, wear out the army and waste supplies, sharing advantage and harm—this is the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Hold divided forces on the defensive, fight when the enemy comes but do not pursue when they withdraw, wearing out our armies and wasting supplies while sharing costs with the enemy—the middling stratagem.

sentences.zh: 若慮餉詘運阻，不敢言戰，則其禍不勝言矣，是謂無策。」

translations.literal: If one fears funds are short and transport blocked and dares not speak of war, then the calamity is beyond words—this is called having no stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: If we fear short funds and blocked supply lines and dare not speak of war, the calamity is beyond description—this is no stratagem at all."

sentences.zh: 補鴻臚寺卿，充​​總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 自此陳說兵事，章凡十三上，多見採納。

translations.literal: From then on he set forth military affairs; in all he submitted thirteen memorials, many of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs, submitting thirteen memorials in all, many of which the court adopted.

sentences.zh: 嗣以中允樊恭煦獲譴，上疏營救，坐鐫秩。

translations.literal: Later, when Junior Mentor Fan Gongxu was punished, he memorialized to rescue him and was demoted in rank as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Junior Mentor Fan Gongxu was punished, he memorialized in his defense and was himself demoted.

sentences.zh: 明年，赴天津佐鴻章與法使巴特納商和約，定新約十款。

translations.literal: The next year he went to Tianjin to assist Hongzhang in negotiating a treaty with the French envoy Patenotre, fixing ten articles of a new agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went to Tianjin to assist Li Hongzhang in negotiating a treaty with the French envoy Patenotre, settling ten articles of a new convention.

sentences.zh: 還，乞歸省。

translations.literal: On his return he requested leave to visit his home.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he asked leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 未出都，命赴廣西與法使會勘中、越分界，至則單騎出關會法使浦理燮。

translations.literal: Before he had left the capital he was ordered to Guangxi to join the French envoy in surveying the Sino-Vietnamese border; on arrival he rode out alone through the pass to meet the French envoy Bourée.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave Beijing he was ordered to Guangxi to survey the Sino-Vietnamese border with the French envoy; on arrival he rode out alone through the frontier pass to meet Bourée.

sentences.zh: 浦理燮欲先勘原界，承修據約先欲改正界限，不相下，乃陽以文淵、保樂、海寧歸我，而陰電其駐京使臣，詆承修違約爭執，謂非先勘原界，勢將罷議。

translations.literal: Bourée wished to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the boundary first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered to return Wenzhou, Baole, and Haining to us, while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to denounce Chengxiu for violating the treaty and contending obstinately, saying that unless the old boundary were surveyed first negotiations would be broken off.
translations.idiomatic: Bourée wanted to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the line first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered Wenzhou, Baole, and Haining to China while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to accuse Chengxiu of violating the treaty, warning that unless the old boundary were surveyed first talks would collapse.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，許之。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, consented.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unable to refuse, agreed.

sentences.zh: 承修遂有三難二害之電奏，略言：「附界居民，不願隸法，先勘原界，慮滋事變，難一。

translations.literal: Chengxiu then sent a telegram memorial setting forth three difficulties and two harms, stating in brief: "Residents along the border do not wish to come under French rule; surveying the old boundary first risks provoking disturbances—the first difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu then telegraphed a memorial listing three difficulties and two harms: "Border inhabitants refuse French rule; surveying the old boundary first risks unrest—the first difficulty.

sentences.zh: 保樂牧馬，游勇獷盛，道路梗阻，難二。

translations.literal: Baole is pastureland; roaming braves are fierce and numerous and block the roads—the second difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Baole is open pasture where roaming braves are fierce and block the roads—the second difficulty.

sentences.zh: 原界碑折，十不存五，巉崗聳巘，瘴雨炎翳，人馬不前，難三。

translations.literal: Old boundary markers are broken; fewer than half of ten remain; steep cliffs tower, malarial rains and blazing mists prevent men and horses from advancing—the third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Old boundary markers are broken—fewer than half remain; sheer cliffs, malarial rains, and suffocating heat stop men and horses—the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 且原界既勘，彼必颺去，新界奚論？

translations.literal: Moreover, once the old boundary is surveyed they will surely cast it aside—what then of the new boundary?
translations.idiomatic: Once the old boundary is surveyed they will surely discard it—what hope for fixing a new line?

sentences.zh: 駈驢、文淵俱不可得，關門失險，戰守兩難，害一。

translations.literal: Neither Qulü nor Wenzhou can be secured; the pass loses its strategic advantage and both offense and defense become difficult—the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Qulü nor Wenzhou can be held; the pass loses its strategic value and both attack and defense become impossible—the first harm.

sentences.zh: 文淵既失，北無寸地，關內通商，勢將迫脅，越既不存，粵將焉保？
